notes.title: Development Update - September 2nd 2025
notes.content: [p]I hope all of you have been enjoying the latest update to Stellar Navigator, and I want to thank everyone who submitted feedback and reported issues during the public beta of v0.4.3. It really made the release process go much smoother, and I look forward to future open beta tests of up coming versions. Your support and contributions mean a lot and make a big difference! So keep an eye out for the next open beta branch.[/p][p][/p][h2]Major Update One[/h2][p]With the minor update out of the way bringing with it a few new features and bug fixes, work has since been started on the first Major Update of Stellar Navigator. This one will come with more planet types, user feedback, and of course the ability to create multiple galaxies. This will lay the ground work for the next major update which will include Steam Workshop support. Remember to follow along with the [url="https://trello.com/b/YTYDvtwl/stellar-navigator-road-map"]public road map[/url] to see any mid-month status changes to features.[/p][p][/p][p]Much the same as was done in the latest version, there will be another conversion script to bring your galaxy into the new multi-galaxy model. As such, this will be another "breaking change" to Stellar Navigator. What this means is once your galaxy file has been converted, older versions of the application will not be able to use them. However, when this update is published, it will open up the scale and freedom of Stellar Navigator as well as bring with it the initial tools for collaborating with your friends![/p][p][/p][p]In later versions there will be further work done to bring the various galaxies you create into a much more exciting format, but for now you can expect the ability to create and load galaxies through a new galaxy selector which will appear on the main menu.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322332/15d33780571836cea8dc39848dd40f5fd17b4dae.png"][/img][/p][p]To give a little more insight into what is being planned for this update and the galaxy selection menu. These are some of the ideas being experimented with to not only allow for the ability for you to create multiple galaxies, but also to give you the tools to define them with your creativity:[/p][list][*][p]Galaxy image selection, use the default galaxy image or add your own.[/p][/*][*][p]Galaxy information, write about what makes this galaxy unique.[/p][/*][*][p]Galaxy type, is it a spiral, Elliptical, Barred, or Irregular?[/p][/*][/list][p][i]Please remember: this is a work in progress and ideas shared may or may not make it into the final update. As always, the focus will be on adding the core functionality to bring you these exciting new updates faster.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]That's it for today - keep an eye out for updates on the official Stellar Navigator Discord server. And as always, keep looking to the stars![/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Development Update - August 4th 2025
notes.content:
[p]Hello everyone!
[/p][p]A lot of effort this month of course went into preparing the first minor release for all of you to try out in the public beta branch. If you haven’t jumped into the public beta branch to try out the new feature, here is what is included:
[/p][p][b]Annotations for star systems.[/b][/p][list][*][p]This allows for custom annotations that can be placed anywhere in the star system (“Solar Navigator”) view.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Entirely revamped marker (“Pin”) system[/b] which should be far easier to use and includes additional features.[/p][list][*][p]Custom pins – You can create your own pin images and place them in the data files for Stellar Navigator to use in your star systems.[/p][/*][*][p]Favoriting pins for quick access.[/p][/*][*][p]Adding text beneath pins to give them more life.[/p][/*][*][p]A conversion script to bring all your existing markers in your solar systems over to the new pin system. Ideally this will provide a seamless method to update your existing work into the new system; however, this is not always a guarantee such are data conversions.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]User Feedback![/b][/p][list][*][p]Clouds can now be toggled on and off.[/p][/*][*][p]Additional data points for orbital period.[/p][/*][*][p]Ability to turn the scanner visual on and off in the galaxy map.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a new setting to the games graphics settings to select which monitor Stellar Navigator should use. This is a potential fix for when some users with multi-monitor set ups are unable to select a resolution. This issue is still under investigation.[/p][/*][/list][p][i]⚠️The minor patch will be released to the live branch on August 29th, 2025. As this is early access, and there’s always a chance for things to go sideways, please back up your game’s data folder in .../My Games/Stellar Navigator… before the 29th. ⚠️[/i][/p][p][i] [/i][/p][p]As for this month’s updates: New planet type designs have moved on prototyping and in some cases implementation! For Major Update One you can expect at least two new planet types based off the fantastic ideas provided by our very own Planetologists![/p][p][/p][p]And as fun as reading can be, let’s look at some visuals:[/p][p][b]Prototyping procedural clouds, and the new lighting effects[/b][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="IagQydKjs-0;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Finally, I am looking through the ideas submitted to the ideas board by the community to see which bits of feedback and ideas could be included in the major update. More on this as the scope of the major update settles down and work begins on the multiple galaxies.[/p][p] [/p][p]Well folks, that’s all for this month! I hope you are all having a wonderful summer and as always keep looking to the stars![/p]

notes.title: Development Update - May 1st 2025
notes.content:
[h1]New marker system in development[/h1]

The existing marker system was created very early on in the development of Stellar Navigator, and as such is showing its age compared to the more recent features that were developed later in the project's life cycle. That being the case, it was one of the first features I wanted to rework post launch of early access. Let's take a closer look at its progress:

[h2]Fluid interaction[/h2]
It was very important for this system to be easy [i]and[/i] quick to use. Marking up the system shouldn't be a difficult task after you have already spent a long time setting up each planet. Therefore, rather than it starting with a window, it starts with a new right click menu that is accessible at any time while in solar navigator.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322332/3435ef88b0d2069d32854823b8b25e41ad815791.gif[/img]


[h2]Introducing Annotations[/h2]
In addition to the easier access to markers and favorited markers, there will be [i]Annotations[/i]. These are a different kind of marker that allow free form text to be placed in areas around a solar system. This way not only can markers be placed, but also information about key areas of a solar system. Below is a mockup of what a label may look like in Stellar Navigator.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322332/f9675c92116ef9bcc8f7f5dcefae134935fd583c.png[/img]

[h1]Community submitted ideas[/h1]
It has and will continue to be my desire to ensure that the community has the ability to provide input into the early access development of Stellar Navigator. I want to ensure that I capture as many of the tools I can to allow user's creativity to be... out of this world!

That said, for the next minor update to Stellar Navigator the following three ideas will be included:
[olist]
[*]An option to turn planet clouds on and off.
[*]Celestial body data point - Orbital Period.
[*]Edit planet radius and orbital radius by entering numeric values.
[/olist]

[h1]🎉Planetologist Winners!!🎉[/h1]
Last month there was a community event held on our Discord server ([url=https://discord.gg/vcPTMpavep]https://discord.gg/vcPTMpavep[/url]) where Navigators submitted a description of their ideal planet to be voted on by the community. Thank you to everyone who submitted a planet and voted. In the end the votes were very close at the top three, so close that two individuals will be working with me to realize their very own ideal planet!

[h2]First place winners![/h2]
[b]StregaRevenge & Thunderbat[/b]

[h2]Second place winner![/h2]
[b]Gameonic[/b]

Congratulations to these winners who's names will be included in Stellar Navigator as Navigator Planetologists. Stay tuned for updates on these new planet types!


Remember to also check out the public road map here: [url=https://trello.com/b/YTYDvtwl/stellar-navigator-road-map]https://trello.com/b/YTYDvtwl/stellar-navigator-road-map[/url] which has seen some changes with the marker system being pushed into development and the above community ideas included as a deliverable of minor update one.

That's all for this month. Until next time, Keep looking to the stars!
